commitResults.messageTitle: Replace address and tags in Person with contexts
commitResults.messageBody:
Person now has a name, optional phone, optional email and a required,
non-empty set of contexts. Address and tags are removed from Person.

- Person: phone and email are Optional; at least one context is required;
  isSamePerson treats two persons as the same when they share a phone or
  an email, and ignores the name.
- Add and edit commands and their parsers use c/ for contexts; add only
  requires a name and at least one context. An empty c/ on edit is rejected.
- Storage: JsonAdaptedPerson saves and loads contexts and allows a missing
  phone or email. Add JsonAdaptedContext.
- UI, messages and sample data show contexts instead of address and tags.
- Update tests, test helpers and JSON test data to match.

Person.MESSAGE_CONTEXT_REQUIRED to say "person" instead of "contact".

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject null contexts in Person and test the saved form of a context
commitResults.messageBody:
The Person constructor now throws NullPointerException if the contexts set
contains a null element, instead of failing later (for example in
Messages.format). Add JsonAdaptedContextTest, which also checks that a context
is saved as a plain string and that the object form is rejected.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make saving safer and keep a backup of an unreadable data file
commitResults.messageBody:
FileUtil.writeToFile now writes to a temporary file and moves it over the
target, so an interrupted save no longer leaves a half-written data file.

When the address book data file cannot be loaded, MainApp copies it to
<name>.bak before starting with an empty address book, so the next save does
not overwrite the original. Add FileUtil.backUp and tests for both changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove the unused logger from PersonListPanel
Recover from null entries in the data file and rename an unreadable file to a timestamped backup
commitResults.messageBody:
A data file with a null inside it (a null person, a null context, or a file
that only contains null) used to escape as a NullPointerException, which was
not caught by the DataLoadingException recovery in MainApp, so the app
crashed at startup. These cases now throw IllegalValueException or
DataLoadingException and take the normal recovery path.

FileUtil.backUp now renames the unreadable data file to
<name>.<UTC time>.bak instead of copying it to <name>.bak. The original name is
free for the next save, and an earlier backup keeps its own name. backUp takes
an optional Clock so tests can fix the time.

Add regression tests and fixture files for the null cases, and update the
backup tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update the User Guide for the new saving behaviour
commitResults.messageBody:
Describe how a save is written, what a saved person looks like in the data
file, and what happens when the data file cannot be read: it is renamed to
addressbook.json.<UTC time>.bak and the app starts empty. Add steps to
recover the data and an FAQ entry for an unexpectedly empty list.
Make saving safer and keep a backup of an unreadable data file

commitResults.messageTitle: Add an archived flag to Person and the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
A Person now knows whether it is archived. The flag is part of equals,
hashCode and toString but not of isSamePerson, so an archived person still
blocks a duplicate phone number or email. Person.withArchived returns a copy
with only the flag changed, and EditCommand keeps the flag when it edits a
person.

The data file gets an optional "archived" key. A missing or null key means
the person is not archived, so existing data files load unchanged. Any value
that is not true or false makes the file unreadable and takes the normal
backup-and-start-empty path.

Nothing in the app uses the flag yet.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the archive, archives and unarchive commands
commitResults.messageBody:
archive INDEX marks the contact at INDEX as archived, so it leaves the normal
contact list but stays in the address book and in the data file. archives
shows only the archived contacts under an "Archives" header, and unarchive
INDEX brings a contact back. Command words are case-insensitive, and INDEX
refers to the list on screen, as for delete.

The normal contact list now shows only contacts that are not archived: list,
add and edit return to it, it is the list shown at start-up, and find searches
only within it. The archives view is the same filtered list with a different
predicate, so no extra view state is stored. unarchive refuses a contact that
is not archived and says to run archives first.

ModelManager exposes whether the archives are shown so that the window can
show the header. The header is shown only for the archives predicate.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep archived contacts safe from clear and edit
commitResults.messageBody:
clear now removes only the contacts that are not archived and goes back to the
normal contact list, so one clear cannot wipe the archive. It says how many
archived contacts were kept.

edit rejects an archived contact and asks the user to unarchive it first.
Before, the edit went through and the contact then disappeared from the
archives view.

delete is unchanged: it removes whichever contact is shown, so it deletes an
archived contact while the archives are shown. Add a test for that.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the archive feature in the User Guide and Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
User Guide: add archive, archives and unarchive, and say how list, find, edit,
delete and clear treat archived persons. Document the optional "archived" key
in the data file and add the new commands to the command summary.

Developer Guide: add use cases UC06 to UC08, describe the archived flag and
the two predicates in the Model and Storage components, add an Archive feature
section with the design alternatives that were considered, add manual test
cases and a glossary entry.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename Person#withArchived to copyWithArchived and drop duplicate tests
commitResults.messageBody:
withX normally means a PersonBuilder method that changes the builder, so
person.withArchived(true) could read as changing the person. copyWithArchived
makes clear that it returns a new Person. PersonBuilder#withArchived keeps its
name, as it does change the builder.

Remove two JsonAdaptedPerson tests that readFromJson_archivedKey_followsTheRules
already covers through real JSON.

commitResults.messageTitle: Address review comments on the archive commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Use "person" in the user-facing messages and usage text of archive, unarchive
and archives, as in DeleteCommand, and rename MESSAGE_NO_ARCHIVED_CONTACTS to
MESSAGE_NO_ARCHIVED_PERSONS.

archives no longer ignores text after the command word, as it is one letter
away from archive and archives 1 is most likely a mistyped archive 1. It now
gives the invalid command format message. Unlike the other commands without
parameters, so it has its own small parser.

Use the renamed Person#copyWithArchived, and make the new tests simpler:
import Person and the assertions instead of using full names, and declare
throws Exception instead of a try/catch.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show specific errors for empty name and context
commitResults.messageBody:
An empty n/ or c/ used to fail the format regex and show the full
constraints message, which lists format rules instead of saying the
value is missing. ParserUtil now rejects a blank name or context with
"Name cannot be empty." / "Contexts cannot be empty." before the
regex check. This also applies to edit, which shares ParserUtil.

INVALID_CONTEXT_DESC was an empty c/, so it is split into
EMPTY_CONTEXT_DESC and a truly invalid c/(orbital).

commitResults.messageTitle: Show specific errors for empty phone and email
commitResults.messageBody:
An empty p/ or e/ now shows "Phone number cannot be empty. Leave out p/
if there is no phone number." (and the same for e/) instead of the
format constraints, matching the ADD spec. The prefixes come from
CliSyntax so the hint stays correct if a prefix changes.

Edit shares ParserUtil, so it shows the same messages. The "leave out"
hint does not fit edit, but edit is outside the MVP.

commitResults.messageTitle: Leave out missing phone and email in result messages
commitResults.messageBody:
Messages.format printed "Phone: ; Email: " for a contact without them.
A missing phone or email is now left out. Contexts are listed first,
each in brackets (e.g. [CS2103T] [Hack&Roll 2026]), followed by phone
and email.

Add MessagesTest, since the command tests build their expected
messages with Messages.format and so cannot catch format changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the clashing person in duplicate add errors
commitResults.messageBody:
A duplicate add showed the generic "This person already exists in the
address book." The message now names the existing person and the
shared value, e.g. "This person already exists: Alex Tan has the same
phone number (91234567)."

UniquePersonList#findDuplicate returns the first person in the list
with the same identity, and is passed up through AddressBook and Model
so AddCommand can build the message. If that person matches on both
phone and email, the message names the phone.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test duplicate add messages and findDuplicate
commitResults.messageBody:
The integration tests check the duplicate message against literal
strings, since building the expected message with the same helper
would pass whatever the helper returns. They cover a phone clash, an
email clash in a different case, a match on both fields (names the
phone), and clashes with several persons (first in the list wins).

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix edit duplicate check and name clashing person
commitResults.messageBody:
The old check skipped the lookup whenever the edited person still
shared a phone or email with the original, so an edit could keep its
own phone but take another person's email. Check the edited person
against every other person instead, and reuse the add error message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep alias, introducer and note when editing
commitResults.messageBody:
EditCommand builds the edited person with the 4-argument Person
constructor, so any edit drops the alias, introducer and note added
to the model in #98, and the loss is saved to the data file.

Let's carry these fields over from the original person. Edit cannot
change them yet; that is left to #110.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test that edit keeps alias, introducer and note
commitResults.messageBody:
No typical person has these fields set, so the existing tests
passed even while edit dropped them.

Let's add a test that edits the phone of a person with all three
fields set. While here, use the indexes and person variables already
in scope instead of get(0) and Index.fromOneBased(1).

commitResults.messageTitle: Add +c/ and -c/ prefixes for editing contexts
commitResults.messageBody:
Edit will add or remove one context at a time instead of replacing
all of them with c/.

Let's define the two prefixes so the edit parser can use them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add and remove single contexts in edit
commitResults.messageBody:
Edit replaces every context with the c/ values, so changing one
context means retyping all of them.

Let's replace c/ with +c/ and -c/, which add or remove one context
at a time. Removals run before additions, so a person's only context
can be swapped and its capitalisation fixed in one command. The
command is rejected if a -c/ context is not found or no context
would remain, and plain c/ is rejected with a hint.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the typed order of edit contexts
commitResults.messageBody:
Contexts are parsed into a HashSet, so an error listing several
unmatched -c/ contexts shows them in an unpredictable order.

Let's use a LinkedHashSet so they keep the order the user typed.
While here, fix the setter Javadocs that still referred to the old
contexts field, and test that +c/ keeps the existing spelling of a
context the person already has.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add -p/ and -e/ prefixes to remove phone and email
commitResults.messageBody:
Phone and email are optional, but edit cannot remove them once set.
An empty p/ or e/ is rejected. Letting it clear the field instead
would wipe the phone if the user presses Enter before typing it.

Let's define explicit remove prefixes so the edit parser can use them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Track phone and email removal in edit descriptor
commitResults.messageBody:
A null phone or email in EditPersonDescriptor means the user did not
type p/ or e/, so it cannot also mean the field should be removed.

Let's add separate flags for removing the phone and email, so the
parser can record -p/ and -e/ and the command can act on them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove phone or email when edit asks for it
commitResults.messageBody:
EditPersonDescriptor can now mark the phone or email for removal, but
createEditedPerson still keeps the old value.

Let's leave the field empty when it is marked for removal, so the
edited person has no phone or email.

Edit can now remove a phone or email, but the parser does not read
the -p/ and -e/ prefixes yet.

Let's parse them and reject -p/ with a value, p/ and -p/ together,
and an empty p/, with the same checks for email. The empty p/ error
now points to -p/, so users know how to remove the field.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test that removing phone and email skips the duplicate check
commitResults.messageBody:
Two people without a phone or email must not count as duplicates,
otherwise removing these fields from a second person would fail.

Let's add a test where both people end up with neither field.

The edit usage message needs to show the new edit prefixes, which
are defined in #116 and #117 but not merged yet.

Let's define the same four prefixes here, identical to those PRs, so
the usage message can use them and the branches merge cleanly.

The usage message still says existing values are overwritten, shows
c/ and does not explain what INDEX is. An edit with no fields shows
only the error, without how to use edit.

Let's show the new parameters, explain INDEX and -p/ / -e/, and add
the usage message to the no-field error.

The edit section still describes address and tags, and says
contexts are replaced.

Let's describe the new format, +c/ / -c/ and -p/ / -e/, with
examples, the success message, duplicates and every error message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add separate phone and email examples to edit errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Rows covering both phone and email errors showed only a phone
example, so the email message had no matching command.

Let's give each message its own example.

Collectors.toSet() does not keep insertion order, unlike the
LinkedHashSet used by ParserUtil.parseContexts. Tests that depend on
context order could then be nondeterministic.

Let's collect contexts into a LinkedHashSet instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Note that phone and email edit parsing mirror each other
commitResults.messageBody:
parsePhoneForEdit and parseEmailForEdit are nearly identical but kept
separate for readability. A future change to one could miss the other.

Let's link the two in their Javadoc so they stay in sync.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix compile and checkstyle errors from edit merges
commitResults.messageBody:
Resolving the merge conflict in EditCommand#equals left a stray
semicolon, so master no longer compiles. The merges also left
trailing whitespace and a misordered import, which fail checkstyle.

Let's remove the semicolon, strip the trailing whitespace and
reorder the import so that the build passes again.
Fix compile and checkstyle errors from edit merges

commitResults.messageTitle: Enable assertions for the run task
commitResults.messageBody:
Gradle enables assertions for the test task by default, but not for
the run task, so assert statements are skipped when the app is
launched via gradlew run.

Let's set enableAssertions for the run task so assertions are checked
during manual runs too.
